MECHANISM (answers 'why predict endpos_logp but not emission'): the two DVs are NEARLY INDEPENDENT across bystanders (emission vs endpos_logp Spearman rho=0.09 p=0.65; rho=0.19 over 28 = #456 H3-miss). They capture different LEAK ROUTES:
- endpos_logp = teacher-forced ※ prob at the fixed trained end-slot (\n\n※). Personas geometrically CLOSE to source (data_scientist cos +0.93, helpful_assistant +0.60, pentester +0.61) inherited the trained end-slot habit -> high logp -> cosine/JS/KL correlate.
- emission_rate = ※ anywhere in a free sample, DOMINATED by structured-output contexts (fammate_format_1 cos -0.47 emis 0.22 logp -4.52; fammate_format_2 cos -0.49 emis 0.21) that leak ※ mid-body, are semantically OPPOSITE the source (negative cosine), and have LOW end-slot logp. So they push emission up at negative cosine -> decouple/anti-correlate emission from the predictors (cos->emission rho=-0.24 N=27).
Net: predictors track the persona-similarity / trained-end-slot route (endpos_logp); the behaviorally-dominant leak is a format-structure route orthogonal to persona geometry.
CAVEAT (deflates the logp side): JS/KL-to-source AND endpos_logp are BOTH read off the model's persona-conditioned next-token distributions -> shared-method variance / partly mechanical, not predictor-vs-independent-outcome. emission is a sampled outcome one step removed. Plus emission floor-compressed+noisy (n=160 near 0.04) lowers power. So 'geometry predicts marker leakage' is NOT supported behaviorally; geometry predicts an end-slot logp readout partly coupled to it by construction.

CORRECTION to the prior mechanism marker (the 'mid-body leak route' claim was WRONG). Inspected raw step-1600 completions: format contexts fire ※ at the trained END-slot, not mid-body (fammate_format_1: 34 end/1 mid; panel-wide only 6/462 firings are mid-body). 

VERIFIED mechanism for emission-vs-endpos_logp decoupling (rho=0.09), from per-context endpos_logp vectors:
1. mean(log p) is dominated by the low-prob tail. fammate_format_1: mean_logp=-4.52 but MEDIAN=-3.12 and frac(p>0.5)=0.24 (=its 0.22 emission); ~76% of its contexts sit near the -18 floor and drag the MEAN down. Source: frac(p>0.5)=0.94, emission 0.90, mean -0.33. So emission tracks the HIGH-prob fraction while the DV (mean log p) tracks the low-prob tail of the SAME skewed per-context distribution.
2. teacher-forced-position vs free-generation: endpos_logp forces 'answer+\n\n' then scores ※; emission needs the model to continue to that position rather than EOS. data_scientist: frac(p>0.5)=0.71 but emission only 0.10 (usually ends the turn instead of appending \n\n※).

NET (more deflating than before): predictors correlate with the MEAN teacher-forced end-slot log p, a position-forced log-averaged quantity dominated by low-prob contexts + forced continuation — largely a measurement artifact of that DV's definition, several steps removed from sampled emission behavior. 'Geometry predicts leakage' remains unsupported behaviorally. Samples: HF issue456_onpolicy/raw_completions/ + eval_results/issue_456/onpolicy_gen/.

CORRECTION: the emission<->endpos_logp decoupling is NOT an aggregation/mean-dominated-by-tail artifact (median + frac decouple from emission just as much). The SOLE driver is teacher-forcing (forcing 'answer + \n\n' then scoring ※) vs free generation (model choosing continue-vs-EOS). Prior 'frac(p>0.5) ~ emission' per-persona match was coincidental (rank rho = -0.04). Net unchanged: teacher-forced end-slot prob (any summary) tracks persona geometry but not behavioral emission. mean(p) on a log y-axis is a marginally cleaner/more-interpretable plot if desired (rho 0.66), same conclusion.
